# Exemptions from the repository-gating check in validate-workflow-gating.sh.
#
# Two formats, and they are not equivalent:
#
#   <basename>                                exempts a whole workflow file
#   <workflow>::<job>::<destination>          exempts one finding
#
# Prefer the second. A bare basename stops the file being scanned at all, so a
# publishing step added to it next year is never seen; a finding key exempts
# exactly what is named and leaves the rest of the file checked.
#
# The bar for either is high. A workflow belongs on this list only if every
# repository running it is *meant* to run the step, and the decision about
# where the artifact goes is genuinely made elsewhere. In almost every other
# case the fix is a `github.repository` gate on the step, or on the `enable=`
# expression of the image target, not an entry here.
#
# Note that being a reusable workflow is not by itself a reason: build.yml is
# called from several places on purpose, but it is also the file that decides
# which registries an image is pushed to, so it is checked.
#
# This is not the baseline. The baseline is debt that shrinks to nothing;
# these are decisions that stay. A line that stops matching anything is
# reported, so an exemption cannot outlive the thing it exempts.
#
# Give every line a reason in a comment above it.

# A pull, not a push. The functional suite authenticates to pull the WAF
# images it tests against; the job publishes nothing. It has to work from both
# repositories, because prep runs the suite against staged images from the
# mirror. The scanner cannot tell a pull login from a push login, and making
# it guess -- by clearing a login when the job has no other detected
# destination -- would silently clear a real push done through a `run:` block.
functional.yml::functional-tests::login:<computed>
